glossary.Acute: Coming on quickly, over hours to days.
glossary.Unilateral: Affecting one side only; bilateral red legs suggest another cause.
glossary.Chronic skin changes: Long-standing damage such as eczema, ulcers or fungal infection that weakens the skin barrier.
glossary.Obesity: Excess body fat, BMI 30 or above.
glossary.Peripheral vascular disease: Narrowed leg arteries giving poor blood flow to the limbs.
glossary.Skin barrier: The outer skin layer that keeps bacteria out.
glossary.Immunocompromised: Having weakened immune defences, from disease or drugs.
glossary.Comorbidity: Another long-term illness the patient also has, e.g. diabetes or heart failure.
glossary.Systemic: Affecting the whole body rather than one area.
glossary.Tachycardia: Heart rate above 100 beats per minute.
glossary.Limb-threatening: Severe enough that the limb could be lost, e.g. from poor arterial supply.
glossary.Blood cultures: Blood samples incubated to grow and identify bacteria in the bloodstream.
glossary.Elevation: Raising the affected limb above heart level to reduce swelling.
glossary.Macrolide: Antibiotic class including clarithromycin and erythromycin, used in penicillin allergy.
glossary.Amoxicillin: A penicillin antibiotic; nausea and diarrhoea are common side effects, not allergy.
glossary.Ceftriaxone: A broad-spectrum IV cephalosporin antibiotic given once daily.
glossary.Surgical consultation: Review by a surgeon to exclude deeper infection such as necrotising fasciitis.
glossary.Vasodilation: Widening of blood vessels, causing redness and warmth.
glossary.Vascular permeability: Leakiness of blood vessel walls, letting fluid out into tissue and causing swelling.
glossary.Neutrophil: The commonest white blood cell, first to arrive and fight bacterial infection.
glossary.Lymphatic channels: Thin vessels that drain tissue fluid towards lymph nodes.
glossary.Regional lymph nodes: The nearby lymph nodes that drain an area, e.g. groin nodes for the leg.
glossary.Lymphatic drainage: Removal of tissue fluid by the lymphatic vessels.
